name: Fort Dearborn — store house

documented_range.note: THE RANGE IS THE FORT'S, NOT THIS BUILDING'S. No source reached dates any individual building inside Fort Dearborn. It opens with the rebuild of 1816 and closes with the demolition of the fort's principal structures in the summer of 1856 (Andreas). What carries the scene date is the middle: the post was garrisoned continuously from June 1832 to 29 December 1836.

position.symbolic_location: Inside the south wall of Fort Dearborn, immediately east of the south gate, fronting north onto the parade.
position.note: READ OFF THE 1830 HARRISON PLAN. Position in pixels on the plate Andreas reproduces at vol. 1 p. 113, scaled at 1.10 ft per pixel (the derivation is on fort_dearborn_palisade and in docs/RESEARCH/fort_dearborn.md section 3), rotated to the sheet's true-north arrow, and hung on the fort centre at local E +1152, N +221. Carry +/-20 percent on the offset from the fort centre and +/-20 m on the fort itself. Hubbard, 1827: 'The store-house and guard-house were on either side of the southern gate'. This record takes the eastern of the two buildings the 1830 plan draws there; the argument for that assignment is on fort_dearborn_guard_house and it rests on where Hubbard's next clause puts the magazine.

footprint.note: NO SOURCE GIVES THIS BUILDING'S SIZE. 12.24 x 4.37 m (about 40 x 14 ft) is the eastern of the two small south-wall buildings as drawn on the 1830 plan at the derived scale. Same warning as its neighbour: the depth is a fourteen-pixel measurement.

kind.note: Hubbard names a store-house beside the southern gate in 1827; Andreas's summary of the rebuilt fort lists a 'provision-store' among what the stockade enclosed. GUARD: Robert Fergus's 1850 account puts a storehouse on the EAST side of the parade with the barracks and the artillery house. That is the compound of the 1850s, twenty years after the pickets came down, and where the 1830 plan and an 1827 eyewitness agree with each other this project follows them.

construction.note: Not stated. Log by the same argument as the barracks.

stories.note: Not attested; single storey is the type for a provision store of this footprint and it is how the 1830 plan draws it.

wall_height_m.note: No height attested. About nine feet: one storey with the head-room a stacked provision store wants.

roof_type.note: Not attested; gable is the type.

roof_pitch_deg.note: No pitch is attested for any building in this fort. 34 degrees is the archetype's mid-range for a shingled or riven-shake roof of this period and span, inferred from construction practice rather than measured.

chimneys.note: A COUNT OF ZERO IS A CLAIM, NOT AN ABSENCE. A provision store is the one building in a fort you do not want a fire in, and nothing describes a stack on this one. The record says none and the model builds none.

function.note: The garrison's provision store. Destroyed with the barracks in the September 1827 lightning fire and standing again on the 1830 plan; see fort_dearborn_barracks for what that does and does not establish.

research_note: The eastern building at the south gate. Nothing distinguishes it from its neighbour in the sources except its name and the side it stands on, and this project's reason for putting it east rather than west is written on fort_dearborn_guard_house.
